parts:
maybe in zoom mode you see sidebands related with the type of weighting you apply before the fft. Maybe you're using Hamming or Hanning ... Try with kaiser-bessel or gaussian. 
It would be helpful if you post the spectrographic image you get.

Gianni

2014-11-27 16:19 GMT+01:00 Kevin Darras <kevind...@gmail.com>:

Hello everyone,

We are carrying out sound propagation measurements with Wildlife acoustics SM2Bat+ units and their ultrasound calibrator in chirp mode at 4m distance. The calibrator is supposed to emit a pulsed signal (chirps) at 40kHz at over 100SPL.

When looking at the spectrogram in Audacity, and zoomed in between 25 and 44 kHz, we see that:

Everything appears normal.

However when generating a zoomed in spectrogram with Seewave's spectro() funciton, we discover additional frequency bands around 28kHz, as well as other bands above 40kHz for the same audio file, and that only when zoomed in:

We are wondering whether these frequency bands are artifacts of the spectrogram generating function or some kind of genuine resonance frequency emitted by the calibrator?

I have uploaded the sample ultrasound file here:
https://drive.google.com/file/d/0B4KjyJcS--yFYjhocGJPNEIxekE/view?usp=sharing

Any help would be greatly appreciated!
Best,

--
Kevin Darras
PhD Student Agroecology

messages.author: bfa183f4897a5619
messages.subject: Re: [seewave] Artifact frequency bands in spectrogram?
parts:
Hi Kevin,

Resampling can introduce weird artifacts, like aliasing. I can't test this without knowing the value of the variable "freq" in your code, but it might be worth playing around with applying a low-pass filter before you resample, to remove any high-frequency harmonics of your pulse, e.g.
 
filtered = ffilter(sound0, from=0, to=freq/2)

best,
jesse
